note: The 7 voters of persona-voters-5lang.json with their 3 production items, Accepts, and Rejects. Each item has the serves and fails lines the user approved on 2026-11-12 (spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-12-council-mode-sheet-v2-test-design.md).

voters.name: Everyday engineer user

cares.serves: Common commands answer well under 300 ms on all 3 OSes.
cares.fails: Start time is near or over the limit, or grows as the tool grows.

cares.serves: One command installs or updates it, with nothing to install first.
cares.fails: The user must install or manage a runtime, package manager, or PATH setup.

cares.serves: Every command has built-in help, and errors say what went wrong and what to do.
cares.fails: Errors show raw stack traces or codes with no next step.

voters.rejects: a runtime they must manage themselves

voters.name: Platform team maintainer

cares.serves: Most of the team can add a command in a day or two with existing patterns.
cares.fails: A new command needs specialist knowledge or long build cycles.

cares.serves: A mature debugger and test framework the team knows, with fast local test runs.
cares.fails: Weak or unfamiliar debugging and testing tools.

cares.serves: The standard library covers most needs.
cares.fails: Core features rely on many third-party packages.

voters.rejects: a codebase only 1 team member can change

voters.name: Future new hire

cares.serves: A newcomer can follow a command's logic without special training.
cares.fails: Following the code needs advanced language or framework knowledge.

cares.serves: Many developers on the job market already know the language.
cares.fails: Few candidates know it, so new hires need long training.

cares.serves: Plenty of current official docs and examples for CLI, HTTP, and OAuth work.
cares.fails: Docs for these tasks are sparse or outdated.

voters.rejects: code that needs specialist knowledge to change

voters.name: Release engineer

cares.item: reproducible builds for 3 OSes from one CI
cares.serves: One CI pipeline builds all 3 OS binaries from the same source.
cares.fails: A release needs a separate machine or manual steps per OS.

cares.item: code signing on macOS and Windows
cares.serves: CI signs and notarizes the artifacts with standard tools.
cares.fails: Signing needs manual steps, or the artifacts are hard to sign.

cares.serves: Each release download is a few megabytes.
cares.fails: Each release ships a bundled runtime or a large download.

voters.rejects: per-OS build machines kept by hand

cares.serves: Few dependencies, pinned versions, and a tool to audit them.
cares.fails: A large or unpinned dependency tree that is hard to audit.

cares.serves: The language prevents buffer overflows and use-after-free in normal code.
cares.fails: Memory errors are possible in normal code.

cares.serves: A toolchain security fix can be rebuilt and released within a week.
cares.fails: Fixes wait on users updating a runtime themselves.

voters.name: Developer-experience support lead

cares.item: the same behavior on all 3 OSes
cares.serves: One codebase behaves the same on all 3 OSes, with no OS branches in common commands.
cares.fails: Paths, shells, or runtimes differ by OS and cause OS-specific bugs.

cares.serves: Errors name the cause and the fix.
cares.fails: Errors are generic or show internals.

cares.serves: One command collects version, environment, and logs for a ticket.
cares.fails: Support must ask users to gather details by hand.

voters.rejects: OS-specific bugs that need per-machine fixes

cares.serves: Low build, run, and maintenance cost over 5 years with the current team.
cares.fails: Hidden costs such as retraining, special build infrastructure, or rewrites.

cares.serves: At least half the current team can maintain it, and replacements are easy to hire.
cares.fails: It depends on 1 or 2 people or a rare skill.

cares.serves: The toolchain has a published support policy that covers 5 years.
cares.fails: The toolchain's 5-year support is uncertain.
